claim: Video anonymisation requires contextual identifiability assessment; blurring/masking and audio treatment are candidate measures, not a universal guarantee.
Face obfuscation can affect video action-recognition utility.
Skeleton trajectories can carry re-identification and sensitive-attribute leakage.
Body proportions and motion style are privacy-relevant skeleton cues.
Learned anonymization can optimize action utility against privacy tasks.
Temporal/video-level privacy attacks matter beyond frame-level handling.
MediaPipe Pose Landmarker supports video-mode frame inference with timestamps.
MediaPipe Face Detector supports video-mode frame inference with timestamps.
MMPose supports configurable image/video inference through a unified inferencer.
FFmpeg supports explicit stream selection and metadata mapping controls.
Learned face anonymizers require task-specific training and evaluation.
